summary:
NASA AgroBot ([https://t.me/nasa_g10_bot](https://t.me/nasa_g10_bot)) is an intelligent agricultural assistant on Telegram, designed to help farms in the Lviv region adapt to climate change by utilizing open-source NASA satellite data.
What we have developed:
We created a chatbot ([https://t.me/nasa_g10_bot](https://t.me/nasa_g10_bot)) that, within 2–3 seconds, provides real-time data on soil moisture (at depths of 0–5 cm and 0–100 cm), temperature, and precipitation, based on the geolocation of a specific field in the Lviv region. The system automatically retrieves data from NASA’s SMAP and GPM satellites via the OPENDAP service and generates user-friendly maps and weekly trend charts.
How this addresses the problem and why it matters:
Due to irregular rainfall and intensive monoculture farming (such as corn and sunflowers), soils are rapidly degrading and losing moisture, while small-scale farmers lack access to expensive monitoring equipment. Our bot makes space-based technologies free and accessible, even to individual local entrepreneurs. This enables farmers to make timely planting decisions and switch to profitable alternatives—such as legumes (soybeans, peas)—that restore soil fertility, maintain water balance, and save 30–40% on fertilizer costs. In the future, the project will scale into a full-fledged AI-based application for personalized crop rotation forecasting.
details:
1. What does it do and how does it work? NASA AgroBot is a Telegram bot that provides farmers in the Lviv region with accurate satellite data on the condition of their fields. The user shares the geolocation of their land plot, after which the system queries NASA's SMAP (soil moisture) and GPM IMERG (precipitation) satellites via the NASA OPENDAP protocol. Within 2–3 seconds, the bot delivers soil moisture levels (at depths of 0–5 cm and 0–100 cm), temperature, precipitation volume, a regional moisture map, and a weekly trend chart.

2. Key Advantages

  • Complete Accessibility: Requires no expensive soil sensors or weather stations—it runs free of charge on a standard smartphone for any smallholder entrepreneur.
  • Instant Speed: OPENDAP data-slicing technology compresses global satellite files from 140 MB down to 67 KB, while one-hour caching ensures fast performance even with weak cellular reception in the field.
  • In-Depth Monitoring: Evaluates moisture not only on the surface but also in the root zone (down to 100 cm).

3. Expected Impact

  • Environmental: Halts soil depletion and preserves water balance by encouraging a shift away from exhaustive monocultures (corn, sunflower) toward sustainable legume alternatives (soybeans, peas, cover crops).
  • Economic: Saves 30–40% on nitrogen fertilizer costsand protects yields against droughts.
  • Future Growth: Scaling into the full-fledged AI-powered AgroSaaS application "My Field" ("Моє Поле"), which will simulate crop rotation strategies with profit calculations ($/ha) and send push notifications for climate risks.
    4. Tools and Technologies
  • Satellite Data: NASA SMAP and GPM IMERG missions.
  • Processing & Backend: NASA OPENDAP service for coordinate filtering, Python programming language, and libraries for geospatial data analysis and chart generation.
  • Interface: Telegram Bot API with one-hour request caching.

5. Project Creativity We transformed complex NASA scientific datasets into a "pocket agronomist" inside a familiar messenger that works in just two clicks. The uniqueness of our solution lies in combining space-based monitoring with an economic strategy for soil fertility restoration.

6. Key Factors Considered by the Team

  • Climate change challenges in the Lviv region (irregular rainfall and drought risks).
  • The impact of intensive monoculture farming on humus degradation and soil desiccation.
  • Weak mobile internet coverage in rural areas (solved by compressing data slices to 67 KB).
  • The limited budgets of independent smallholder farmers.
